annotations.text:
Two separate complaints, two separate fixes.

UGLY / looks AI-built — the current palette is #a238ff violet on #16161d with system-ui and 10px radii. That is the house style of every AI-generated app. Three replacements below.

MAKES NO SENSE — eight peer tabs for what is really four entry points and a three-stage pipeline. Fixed the same way in all three directions, because it is not a matter of taste.

A — CONSOLE (shown at full size)

For: it reads as a tool, not a product. Dense enough to see the whole queue at once, mono for anything you compare (budgets, track counts, paths), one amber that only ever means "this needs you".

Against: unfriendly to a newcomer. Warm near-black is still dark — if the objection was dark itself, pick B.

B — EDITORIAL

For: paper-light, serif headings, the furthest thing from an AI app. Music libraries suit it; long release titles read better.

Against: least dense of the three — more scrolling on a 200-row request table. Light UI at night is a real cost if you work late.

C — STUDIO

For: closest to what you have, so the smallest leap. Slate-teal and citron instead of violet-on-charcoal kills the generic look without changing the shape of anything.

Against: still recognisably a dark app with cards and rounded corners. If "looks like every AI app" is the main objection, this is the weakest answer to it.

WHAT I NEED FROM YOU

1. Which direction — A, B or C. I will take the winner to full fidelity across every screen.

2. Static mockups, or working prototype? These are static. A prototype would let you click through the whole pipeline before I touch the real CSS.

Nothing here is in the app yet. The .dc.html sources are committed to the branch.
